title: Pemvidutide: GLP-1/Glucagon Dual Agonist for Obesity and MASH — Research Dossier
excerpt: Pemvidutide (ALT-801) is Altimmune’s once-weekly GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist with Phase 2b MASH data (55% liver fat reduction at EASL 2026) and Phase 3 PERFORMA trial launched in August 2026. Its glucagon component drives hepatic fat oxidation and thermogenesis that pure GLP-1 agonists lack.

Research compounds discussed for educational purposes. Not FDA-approved for human use where applicable. Consult a healthcare provider before use.

What Is Pemvidutide?

Pemvidutide (ALT-801) is an investigational once-weekly injectable peptide developed by Altimmune that co-activates both GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) receptors and glucagon receptors. This dual mechanism distinguishes it from semaglutide and other pure GLP-1 receptor agonists: the added glucagon receptor component specifically drives hepatic fat oxidation, increases energy expenditure through thermogenesis, and mobilizes stored fat from the liver — making it particularly promising not just for obesity, but for metabolic-associated steatohepatitis (MASH).

Mechanism of Action

Pemvidutide’s two-receptor strategy targets metabolic disease through complementary pathways:

  • GLP-1 receptor activation: Slows gastric emptying, enhances glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon (in the pancreas), and reduces appetite via hypothalamic circuits.
  • Glucagon receptor activation: Increases hepatic glucose production (counterbalanced by the GLP-1 insulin effect), drives fatty acid oxidation in the liver, and activates thermogenesis via brown adipose tissue and FGF21 signaling. This pathway is the primary driver of its MASH-specific effects — glucagon receptor agonism directly mobilizes hepatic fat in a way GLP-1 agonism alone does not.

The balance between these two opposing pathways (GLP-1 drives insulin up, glucagon drives glucose up) is carefully calibrated in pemvidutide’s molecular design to produce net metabolic benefit without hyperglycemia.

Key Research Findings

Phase 2 MOMENTUM Trial (Obesity)

  • Design: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; n=391 adults with overweight or obesity without T2D
  • Duration: 48 weeks
  • Highest dose (2.4 mg weekly): 15.6% body weight reduction
  • Notable finding: lean mass preservation — the majority of weight lost was fat mass, with relative sparing of muscle, a key differentiator from some other weight-loss approaches
  • LDL cholesterol reductions also observed

Phase 2b IMPACT Trial (MASH, EASL 2026)

  • 48-week data presented at the European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL) Annual Meeting 2026
  • Dose 1.8 mg weekly: approximately 55% liver fat reduction vs. approximately 8% on placebo
  • MASH resolution (histologically confirmed) observed in a meaningful proportion of treated patients
  • These liver-specific effects reflect the glucagon-driven hepatic fat mobilization that distinguishes pemvidutide from pure GLP-1 agonists

Phase 2 RECLAIM Trial (Alcohol Use Disorder)

  • Topline results reported July 2026
  • Explored GLP-1/glucagon co-agonism in alcohol use disorder, an emerging indication for GLP-1-class drugs
  • Full data analysis pending publication

Phase 3 PERFORMA Trial (MASH)

  • Enrollment began August 2026
  • Large-scale confirmatory trial for MASH/liver fibrosis endpoints
  • Results will be the critical regulatory data package for a potential MASH indication

Dosing in Research

In clinical trials, pemvidutide has been tested at 0.6 mg, 1.2 mg, 1.8 mg, and 2.4 mg administered as once-weekly subcutaneous injections. These are investigational doses from controlled trials and do not constitute prescribable or safe doses for unsupervised human use. Pemvidutide is not approved by any regulator and is available only within clinical trials.

Frequently Asked Questions

What makes pemvidutide different from other GLP-1 drugs for weight loss?

The glucagon receptor component drives hepatic fat oxidation and thermogenesis that pure GLP-1 agonists lack. This may explain pemvidutide’s particularly strong liver-fat-reduction effect (55% in MASH) and its pattern of lean mass preservation during weight loss. For individuals with significant liver fat accumulation, pemvidutide may be mechanistically superior to GLP-1 mono-agonists, though no direct head-to-head trial has been published.

What is MASH and why is pemvidutide being studied for it?

MASH (metabolic-associated steatohepatitis, formerly known as NASH) is inflammatory liver damage driven by fat accumulation, insulin resistance, and oxidative stress. It affects millions of people worldwide and can progress to cirrhosis and liver cancer. Pemvidutide’s glucagon receptor agonism directly targets hepatic fat — the root pathology of MASH — making it mechanistically well-suited as a MASH therapy. Phase 2b IMPACT data showing 55% liver fat reduction represent some of the strongest hepatic-effect data for any GLP-1-class agent.

Has pemvidutide been approved anywhere?

No. Pemvidutide is fully investigational as of October 2026. It is in Phase 3 development for MASH (PERFORMA trial) and has completed Phase 2 trials in obesity and MASH. Regulatory submissions will depend on the Phase 3 results, which are not yet available.

Research Limitations

  • Phase 3 efficacy and safety data are not yet available; PERFORMA trial started August 2026
  • MOMENTUM obesity data are company-reported; peer-reviewed publication status should be verified
  • The MASH histological response rates (not just liver fat %) need full publication for complete evaluation
  • Long-term cardiovascular outcomes data are absent
  • Most published Phase 2 data come from company conference presentations, not yet primary peer-reviewed journals
  • RECLAIM (AUD) topline results have not been fully published as of October 2026
